body:
Port the clean dual-affine DP kernel to a shared 16-lane implementation for ARM64 NEON and x86 SSE4.1. Static, adaptive and shifted-band dispatch now lets these backends follow the existing clean AVX2 semantics rather than the legacy rounded-band fallback.

- Shared byte-vector operations and kernel logic for NEON/SSE4.1.
- SSE4.1 selection on x86 without AVX2; `BONEFISH_FORCE_SSE=1` permits comparisons on AVX2 machines.
- 3,000 deterministic DP cases, scalar static-band comparisons, SSE4.1/AVX2 comparisons, and a common result/CIGAR digest across native platforms.

## Tested head and native validation

Tested exact head: `c1b7eb074b49806a86bbd0e48c617957ac436618`, against main `e8034d93ad7d7d213979147d648baaf98623117c`. No branch source edits or commits were made during testing.

- **Native CI passed on x86 Linux, ARM Linux and Apple Silicon**: [run 38478508116](https://github.com/DylanCosto/bonefish/actions/runs/38478508116). The SSE4.1/AVX2 comparisons and shared 3,000-case DP digest passed.
- Local M4 Pro: **142 Rust tests passed** (131 core, 5 integration, 6 doctests); three existing benchmarks ignored. **13 Python checks** and the existing evidence consistency checks passed.
- Existing end-to-end SAM/PAF variants, raw-index equivalence, BAM/FASTQ/BGZF input and native sorted-BAM fixture checks passed.

## Paired nominal-1x HG002 ONT WGS

Same 86,553 reads / 3,088,602,282 sequenced bases, complete GRCh38 no-alt reference, compiler/profile/features, eight threads and SAM destination filesystem. Input is the existing equal-base file-order prefixes of four public HG002 R10.4.1 ultra-long source runs, Dorado 0.4.0 SUP 4.1.0; it is not a uniform random sample.

Generic ARM64 release, rustc 1.98.1, jemalloc, opt-level 3, fat LTO, one codegen unit; no native CPU tuning flags. Timer includes fresh FASTA-built index, mapping and SAM writing. FASTQ and SAM are on the **internal APFS SSD**; reference is on the external SSD for both builds. Input hashing/inventory and all output checks occur outside timing.

| Build | Trials | Mean elapsed | Range |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Current main / older ARM DP | 3 | 146.492 s | 132.658-170.340 s |
| neon-clean-dp | 3 | 121.805 s | 115.940-130.570 s |

Observed mean elapsed reduction: **16.85%** (1.203x throughput ratio). Summed worker alignment duration fell **25.20%** and retired instructions **22.40%**. Worker durations are wall-time sums across reads, not exact CPU shares. Trial order was control-1, candidate-1, candidate-2, control-2, control-3, candidate-3. All trials are included. This is a small sample on one Mac under current memory/storage conditions, not a general performance guarantee or a comparison against the earlier day's 106.9-second mean.

## Output checks and changes

Every run passed exact primary inventory and orientation-restored sequence/quality checks. Outputs were deterministic within each build. The complete first pair additionally passed CIGAR consumption/SEQ lengths, reference bounds and identical reference-header checks; its hashes match the repeats.

- Both builds: **86,553 unique primaries; 77,376 mapped, 9,177 unmapped; no missing/extra input reads or mapping-status changes.**
- Records: **132,946 -> 133,778** (832 additional non-primary records).
- **3,538 reads have changed record multisets**, including **3,094 changed primary records**.
- **124 both-mapped primary chromosome/strand placements changed**; 1,095 primary positions, 1,920 primary CIGARs and 682 primary MAPQs changed (categories overlap).

Normalized SAM SHA256, excluding `@PG`:

- Main on this Mac: `4004e1b32a5515b8d006fa16dec0323f56af1c4938cabfbfbb3f0805829d4c66`
- Branch on this Mac: `48da0e7d35654db9f6d3d45c171def634802c6ae4830b25c1fe06af54ff288d8`

Dataset SHA256: `960490bd561a62a82551a729abd97ed5f8fb27a228287b44c9fb6378b65b8116`.
Reference SHA256: `3c8def6d325c5d1e934b2dd530c4d1709f027677a15859467071fddf3fff2026`.
Tested Mac executable SHA256: `40bfeb7053a0da22d1ce2a7709e77d441b9ca719afc684e949c38fd211109662`.

These results establish agreement on the shared native DP fixtures and structural preservation on real Mac data. **They do not preserve every older ARM alignment.** The branch replaces that legacy behavior with clean/adaptive semantics intended to match x86 AVX2. A full real-WGS x86/ARM replay and independent GIAB/variant-calling accuracy assessment remain separate checks; neither was performed here. The branch SAM hash above provides the expected result for a native replay with the exact recorded inputs/options.

Clean dispatch covers NEON and AVX2/SSE4.1 for supported non-generic dual-affine scoring. CPUs lacking both x86 features, and generic-scoring paths, retain legacy fallbacks.

Detailed trial JSON/logs, changed-read summaries, output-comparison results and the tested Mac executable are retained locally under `outputs/bonefish-neon-clean-dp/`. The first full control/candidate SAM pair remains in internal scratch; later SAMs were discarded only after complete validation and recording their hashes. No large test data was pushed. This PR remains a draft for review; no merge was made.
title: Port clean dual-affine DP to NEON and SSE4.1
